title: Silent `preload()` failure inside a `class_name` when trying to load a scene that references an autoload that references the `class_name` and is later in the list of autoloads than another autoload that preloads that scene
body:
### Tested versions

4.1 to 4.6

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (ADL GT2) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1235U (12 threads) - 15.34 GiB memory

### Issue description

The title may be confusing, so to visualize it a bit, the setup looks like this:
- 1st autoload ---(preloads)---> scene ---(references)---> 2nd autoload ---(references)---> StaticScript ---(preload FAIL)---> scene

The fact that the order of the two autoloads matters makes me believe that this isn't a personal error with cyclic references, but an error in how the engine handles this situation. To make it clear, the following does work:

- 2nd autoload ---(preloads)---> scene ---(references)---> 1st autoload ---(references)---> StaticScript ---(preload SUCCESS)---> scene

(As in, same scripts, just swapping their order in the Globals menu)

I found this when trying to instantiate such a failed preload scene, resulting in this error: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/89cea143987d564363e15d207438530651d943ac/scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp#L171


### Steps to reproduce

Check out the MRP.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[TrulyDiabolicalPreloadIssue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25142971/TrulyDiabolicalPreloadIssue.zip)
